alternative_explanations: The high masses of millisecond pulsars are explained by standard stiff EoS combined with rotational support (exceeding the static TOV limit) due to binary spin-up, without requiring any relaxation of the fundamental nuclear EoS axioms.
assumptions: The static equilibrium axioms of the dense matter equation of state can be formally relaxed to permit mass accumulation beyond the static Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit via rotational and thermal support without violating the causality bound.
Binary mass accretion and angular momentum transfer can be modeled as a continuous thermodynamic and mechanical perturbation that modifies the effective equilibrium conditions of the neutron star.
Companion ablation primarily affects the surface and magnetosphere, allowing the core mass-spin relation to remain governed by the relaxed effective equilibrium axioms.
boundary_conditions: The claim fails if the relaxed static equilibrium axioms violate the causality bound, or if the predicted mass-spin relation contradicts the observed population of massive millisecond pulsars, or if standard rotational support models fully explain the observations without needing the relaxed axioms.

allowed_support_kinds: At least one causal pathway connecting collapse inputs to a magnetized rotating neutron star.
Admit works that propose, simulate, or test a physical mechanism for pulsar formation; exclude purely descriptive catalogs without mechanism.
claim_limits: Does not present specific observational data or simulation results on pulsar birth spins or magnetic field strengths.
Does not establish discriminative criteria between successful pulsar formation and failed/black-hole collapses.
Does not validate or test specific magnetohydrodynamic or dynamo mechanisms for field amplification.

falsifiers: A result showing the stated gap is resolved without this hypothesis, or a formal proof that the relaxed axioms inevitably violate causality or tidal deformability constraints, or that standard rotational support fully accounts for the mass-spin relation without relaxing the static axioms.
